title: Chutes AI Automation Setup in 2026: Steps, Limits, Fixes
summary: Chutes AI automation means workflow tools send OpenAI-style requests on triggers and write responses for you.
body_markdown:
## Stage 3: schedule it with a workflow tool


Schedule it by having a timer fire the same HTTP POST you just tested, with the same key and model name, then write the reply somewhere you'll actually look. The call doesn't change, only what triggers it and where the answer lands.


Set the frequency against your plan's request limit first. A schedule that fires faster than the limit allows won't fail loudly. It'll return rejections on some runs and succeed on others, and the gaps look like flakiness.


### Option A: cron or a hosted function


If you already have a server, cron is the shortest path. One line fires a script that posts to the endpoint, and the key sits in an environment variable on that machine.


> A schedule that fires faster than the limit allows won't fail loudly. It'll return rejections on some runs and succeed on others, and the gaps look like flakiness.


Retries are yours to write, so a failed run stays failed until you add a loop.


Take away the server and you have a hosted function (a small piece of code a cloud provider runs on a timer). It keeps the key in the provider's secret store and usually brings its own retry setting.


The cost is a deploy step and one more dashboard to check when a run goes quiet.


### Option B: a workflow tool with an HTTP step


With a no-code workflow tool you get a schedule trigger, an HTTP step where you paste the endpoint, headers and JSON body, and a retry toggle on that step.


Put the key into the tool's connection or secrets store rather than into a file. That makes it quick to start and awkward to review, because the logic lives in screens instead of a diff.


Read the retry column most carefully: it tells you who is responsible when a cold start makes the first attempt fail.


Approach Setup time Retry handling Where the API key lives Best for


Cron Shortest if you own a server None unless you write it Environment variable on the host One fixed job on a machine you already run


Hosted function Moderate; needs a deploy Often a platform setting Provider's secret store Code you want versioned without a server


No-code workflow tool Short; fill in a form Toggle on the HTTP step The tool's connection store Non-developers and multi-step flows


[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/) can be the scheduler here, with one caveat: it has no dedicated Chutes integration, so you reach Chutes through its generic HTTP step, the same request as the curl test.


That suits this job, because a platform that resells you a model has picked and priced it before you open the product, while here the model is whatever name you copied from the Chutes list and the spend lands on your own Chutes balance at Chutes' rates.


**Bring-your-own-key starts on the $20 Plus plan** , which includes 10,000 credits a month and counts a run as 1 credit however many steps it has, so cost doesn't increase with automation complexity, and MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run Activepieces in production.


The Plus line on the pricing page lists bring-your-own AI keys at $0.007 a credit once you pass the 10,000, which is the rate to set against what a reselling platform charges for its own bundled model, so a customer can see whether bringing their own saves money.


In the JSON response, the reply text sits in the first choice's message content. Map that one field to a spreadsheet row or a chat message, and add a timestamp column. When a run goes missing, that column shows you the gap.
